entries.note: Source 607 'SECOND SENATOR' (the tag has no period) is followed by the speech at 608-612, with DUKE. next at 614. The proposed body is character-identical to the served inner text and to source 608-612. The only changes are removing the brackets and adding the tag's period, in both editions. The label now matches the FIRST SENATOR. style and passes the reader's speaker-label rule.

Source 715 has the joint tag 'DUKE and SENATORS.', then 716 'Dead?', with BRABANTIO. answering at 718. Only the brackets are removed, since the label was already inside them. The reader's label rule accepts the lowercase connector 'and', so the joint label renders as a speaker.

Source: OTHELLO. 810, then 811, then [_Exeunt Iago and Attendants._] 813, then 815-819 as Othello continues to the Senate. DUKE. follows at 821. The body matches the served text and the source exactly, and the modern keeps the candidate's words.

No change is correct. At source 1291, '[_Within._] A sail, a sail, a sail!' comes after a blank line with no speaker tag, so it is not Cassio's. The cry already sits outside the bracket, so no speaker should be invented. Missed case 6.61 is analogous.
Source: CASSIO. 1323, then 'Enter second Gentleman.' 1330, then 1332, where Cassio questions the returning Gentleman, who answers at 1334. The body is exact in both editions.
Source: CASSIO. 1349, then the entrance at 1360, then 1362-1367, where Cassio greets Desdemona. She replies 'I thank you, valiant Cassio' at 1369-1370. The body is exact.
No change is correct. Source 1380 '[_Within._] A sail, a sail!' is unattributed: it follows Desdemona's line after a blank line, with no tag.

Source: CASSIO. 1392, then [_Exit Gentleman._] 1395, then 1397-1400. The inline '[_To Emilia._]' is kept exactly as served and as in the source. It renders as an italic cue and does not create a false speaker label. After the fix, 4.47 and 14.80 will be the only speeches in the edition that keep an inline cue, because the served parser stripped the source's other inline cues from ordinary speeches (e.g. 3.24 [To Brabantio], 4.77 [Aside]). Keeping it is faithful and helpful. No change is needed.

Source: IAGO. 1526, whose aside runs 1527-1534, then [_Trumpets within._] 1536, then 1538. This line is spoken aloud, since Cassio answers '’Tis truly so.' at 1541. A plain IAGO. prefix, not an aside, is right. Served 4.77 had already lost its [Aside.] cue; that is out of scope.

Source: IAGO. 1845, then 'Some wine, ho!' 1846, then [_Sings._] 1847, then the song at 1849-1853. The italic markers are kept, so 'IAGO. _..._' matches the 13.25/13.32 song convention. The served parser had already dropped the [_Sings._] cue at 1847 from 6.28. As a result, 6.28-6.30 become three consecutive IAGO paragraphs with the song marked only by italics; Cassio's 'an excellent song' follows. That is acceptable. Restoring the cue would need an out-of-scope change to 6.28.
Source 1855 'Some wine, boys!' is spoken by Iago after the song, before CASSIO. at 1857. No direction intervenes: the split comes from the song block. The body is exact.
Source: IAGO. 1879, then [_Sings._] 1882, which is kept as served paragraph 6.38, then the song at 1884-1891. The italics are kept and the song convention is followed. The body is exact.
Source 1893 'Some wine, ho!' is spoken by Iago after the song, with CASSIO. next at 1895.
Source: IAGO. 2017, with an aside to Roderigo at 2018, then [_Exit Roderigo._] 2020, then 2022-2024 called aloud to the fighters. A plain prefix is right.
Source: [_A bell rings._] 2026, then 2028-2030 as Iago continues, then Othello enters at 2032. The body is exact.
Source: OTHELLO. 2146, then 'Enter Desdemona, attended.' 2152, then 2154-2155. The first sentence is about Desdemona and the second is addressed to Cassio. DESDEMONA. replies at 2157.
Source: OTHELLO. 2160, then [_Montano is led off._] 2166, then 2168-2171, addressed to Iago and Desdemona. [_Exeunt..._] follows at 2173.
Source: IAGO. 2279 (soliloquy), then 'Enter Roderigo.' 2308, then 2310, where Iago greets him. RODERIGO. follows at 2312.
Source: IAGO. 2319, then [_Exit Roderigo._] 2334, then the soliloquy at 2336-2342, then [_Exit._] 2344.
Source: CASSIO. 2420, then [_Exit Clown._] 2423 and 'Enter Iago.' 2425, then 2427. IAGO. replies at 2429.
Source: CASSIO. 2445, then [_Exit Iago._] 2448, then 2450-2451 spoken with Cassio alone, before 'Enter Emilia.' at 2453.
Source: OTHELLO. 3039, then 3040 'Your napkin is too little;', then the direction at 3042, then 3044. DESDEMONA. follows at 3046. The continuation reads well standalone.
Source: IAGO. 3115, then [_Exit Emilia._] 3119, then the soliloquy at 3121-3129. The body is exact.

Source: EMILIA. 3632, then 'Enter Cassio and Iago.' 3638, then 3640. IAGO. follows at 3642.
Source: DESDEMONA. 3691, then [_Exit Iago._] 3694, then 3696-3710, addressed to Emilia. EMILIA. follows at 3712. The body is exact across all 15 lines.

Source: CASSIO. 3759, whose line 3763 ends 'Sweet Bianca,', then [_Giving her Desdemona’s handkerchief._] 3765, then 3767. This continues Cassio's sentence mid-way, and it reads fine as a standalone speech. Besides the prefix, the modern's only change is capitalizing 'Copy'.
Source: IAGO. 3929, then 'Enter Cassio.' 3936, then 3938. CASSIO. follows at 3940.
Source: IAGO. 3950, then [_Exit Cassio._] 3959, then 3961, addressed to the reviving Othello. OTHELLO. follows at 3963.
Source: IAGO. 4017, then [_Othello withdraws._] 4021, then 4023-4029. This is Iago's soliloquy while Othello is hidden, and PG gives no aside cue.

Source: 'Enter Cassio.' 4031, then 4033-4036. The first sentence works as an aside, though PG does not mark it. The closing question is addressed to Cassio, who answers at 4038. A plain IAGO. prefix is faithful to the source.
Source: OTHELLO. 4391, then [_Exit Desdemona._] 4402, then 4404-4406, addressed to Lodovico, then [_Exit._] 4408.
Source: OTHELLO. 4501, then [_Exit Emilia._] 4504, then 4506-4509 with Othello alone, then Desdemona and Emilia enter at 4511.

Source: OTHELLO. 4644, whose line 4647 ends '—You, mistress,', then 'Enter Emilia.' 4649, then 4651-4654, addressed to Emilia, then [_Exit._]. The original opens with the dependent clause 'That have the office...' because the source splits the sentence at the entrance. With the prefix and the preceding [Enter Emilia.] it still reads, and no words can be added to the original. The modern adds 'You,', the only added word in the proposal. It gives the speech a proper standalone opening and follows 12.45's closing '— You, madam,' naturally.
Source: IAGO. 4814, then [_Trumpets within._] 4817, then 4819-4821, addressed to Desdemona.
Source: [_Exeunt Desdemona and Emilia._] 4823 and 'Enter Roderigo.' 4825, then 4827. RODERIGO. follows at 4829.
Source: DESDEMONA. 5036, then the song at 5038-5044 (served 13.25), then 5046 'Lay by these:—', spoken to Emilia.

Source: [_Sings._] 5048, then '_Sing willow, willow, willow._' 5049. The proposal drops the '[Sings.]' cue and restores the source's italics. This entry and 13.29 are the only places where served words (the cue) are removed. That follows the stated convention (13.25/13.32 also omit the Singing/Sings cue), and the sung words are exact. Confirmed, with this caveat.
Source 5051 is a spoken line between the two sung fragments. The body is exact.

Source: [_Sings._] 5053, then the italic song at 5054-5055. This gets the same treatment and caveat as 13.27. The closing '_' after the dash still parses as emphasis, the same pattern that ends candidate 13.25.

Source 5057 is spoken, with EMILIA. following at 5059. Together with 13.26-13.29, this gives six consecutive DESDEMONA paragraphs that alternate song (italic) and speech. That is accurate, and merging them is not possible without shifting paragraph indices.
Source: DESDEMONA. 5062, then [_Sings._] 5063, then the song at 5064-5066 (served 13.32), then 5068-5069 spoken. The split comes from the song block, not from a direction.
Source: IAGO. 5422, then [_A chair brought in._] 5425, then 5427-5431. It keeps the source's inline '[_To Bianca_]', which has no period in the source either. The same note as 4.47 applies.

Source: OTHELLO. 5498, then [_Kissing her._] 5515, then 5517-5523. DESDEMONA. follows at 5525.

Source 6056 'OTHELLO' (the tag has no period) is followed by 6057-6058, then [_Iago stabs Emilia..._] at 6060. The only changes are removing the brackets and adding the period, in both editions.

missed.why: This is not a defect, and no change is recommended. It is an offstage cry inside a direction, printed exactly as the source prints it (line 1980 [_Cry within_: “Help! help!”]), with no speaker named. Like 4.18 and 4.41 it should stay as it is. It is listed only so that the related-cases set is complete. The candidate has the same paragraph.

summary: Verdict: all 47 entries are confirmed. All four checks are true for every entry, and no entry needs a change. Speakers: each of the 45 changed paragraphs is attributed to the nearest preceding source tag, with no other tag in between. 4.18 and 4.41 are correctly left without a speaker. Original-en: every proposed body matches the served text inside the brackets character for character, and matches the cited source lines joined with single spaces. The only other changes are the added prefix, the periods added to the 3.4 and 15.146 tags, and, in 13.27 and 13.29, dropping the '[Sings.]' cue and restoring the source's italics under the stated song convention. Modern-en: every proposed text matches the candidate (sha 012ede1e) apart from the prefix and bracket removal, the capital in 10.93 and 'You,' in 12.47. All 453 excerpt lines quoted in the proposal match pg1531.txt. Coverage: a word-level alignment of the whole source play against the served edition (26,340 vs 26,341 words) found 8 differences, all explained by tag words inside brackets and dropped Sings/Singing cues. Besides the 47 entries, it found no spoken or sung text in a bracketed or unlabeled paragraph, except the source-bracketed cry at 6.61. Every labeled paragraph's speaker matches the source. The candidate has the same bracket and label layout as the original (0 differences). A Python port of the reader's speaker-label rules yields exactly one label, the intended prefix, on all 90 proposed texts. Minor notes, none requiring action: (a) 13.27 and 13.29 drop '[Sings.]', as the convention intends. (b) The served 6.28 had already lost the source's [_Sings._] (line 1847), so the first song is marked only by italics. (c) The original 12.47 opens with the dependent clause 'That have the office...', which is unavoidable without adding words. (d) 4.47 and 14.80 keep inline cues that the parser stripped from every other speech. Integration notes for whoever applies it: the currently served live othello-modern-en.json has the same 47 paragraphs bracketed at the same indices. Paragraph indices do not change, but the new text invalidates artifacts pinned to the old text: the modern lines sidecar (26 affected paragraphs have offsets), the character-card paragraphHashes and 34 mentions in 22 affected paragraphs, and any original-en lines or audio word-timing sidecars. These need to be regenerated.
